Harrisonburg police investigating brandishing incident at party

By Michael Russo
Published: Sep. 8, 2026 at 10:45 AM EDT|Updated: 17 hours ago
Add Us On GoogleAdd as a preferred source on Google
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:39
Instaread

HARRISONBURG, Va. (WHSV) - Harrisonburg police are investigating a brandishing incident that happened at a party in the city on Aug. 23.

The incident happened Saturday, Aug. 23, in the 1300 block of South Main Street, according to the Harrisonburg Police Department, between the intersections with Port Republic Road and South Avenue. This was a week before a separate brandishing incident that was reported the same night as a shooting at The Harrison on Devon Lane on Saturday, Aug. 29.

HPD described the suspect as a shorter white man with a skinny build and a brown “mop”-style haircut. He had goatee-style facial hair and was wearing a black T-shirt, dark pants and dark shoes. HPD said he first arrived at the party with three other men around 11:44 p.m, speaking with party organizers before they were kicked out. The suspect returned alone wearing a black Hollister hoodie about 25 minutes later, when party organizers confronted him again, HPD added.

Autoplay
1 of 5

After an argument, HPD said, the suspect pulled back his jacket and showed what witnesses described as a black assault rifle-style rifle in his waistline, with the barrel pointed down toward the ground inside his pants. The suspect then left the area on foot heading south toward South Avenue, HPD said.

This incident is still an active, open investigation. HPD asked anyone with information about the incident to call 540-434-4436 and ask to talk with Detective Burrows. Tips can also be submitted online. Both methods are anonymous, HPD said, and information that leads to a suspect’s arrest may be eligible for a reward through Crime Solvers.
